lists.grade: Core-ladder silhouettes are genuinely Watabou-competitive (town PASSes outright; thorp, hamlet, year-018/100 read), but §591 totality fails today: the four history leaves are visually the base map (2-26 changed elements of ~1089), the flagship metropolis reads unfinished, ports and high relief don't read, and relict walls float as law-breaking slashes.

findings.fixShape: Give demoted/relict rings a real dressed style (old-wall double line with ends anchored on gates or district edges) or suppress fragments below a coherence threshold; lives in the wall/ring band renderer on the register path.

findings.title: History/scenario leaves are visually indistinguishable from their base map — the §612 product doesn't reach the page

Must land before more waves stack on the scenario system.

findings.title: Metropolis value hierarchy collapses — ~60% of the flagship leaf reads as un-inked ghost fabric
findings.evidence: Viewed metropolis-metropolis-parchment at 1400px: center/south fabric is near-paper-value pale blocks against a saturated brown N arc — reads as pencil underlay or ruins on a 'Comfortable, 71,325 souls' page. 320px squint inverts hierarchy: the map reads as a dense crescent around a pale VOID, the void being the strongest shape.

findings.title: Ports don't read on either port leaf — no quay, no legible piers, fjord fabric retreats from the water
findings.evidence: city declared 'coast, port, plural squares'; fjord declared 'mountain + ocean + port' (manifest.json). Zoom crop review654/zoom/city-harbor.png: one small black pier-blob plus rows of outlined tan squares floating in the water — confetti even zoomed, no quay line. fjord 1400px: a broad empty strand separates ALL fabric from the waterline; no waterfront street; squint reads 'town avoiding the sea'.
findings.fixShape: Waterfront treatment in the water-interface stage: hard quay line where fabric meets harbor water, pier geometry with real visual weight, and a shore-hugging waterfront street that pulls fabric to the water on port leaves.

findings.title: High-relief terrain dress reads as pen noise; scribble-mesh/zigzag glyphs read as errors
findings.evidence: Viewed town-2/fjord (relief 1.00) and mountain-village (0.66): terrain is stochastic scratch/claw/twig-star ticks with no ridge, valley, or terrace structure — mountain-village's declared 'terraced siting' is invisible, left 60% of that leaf reads as blank scrub. Separate artifact family confirmed: crosshatch mesh floating in hamlet fields (~1050-1100,290-430), mountain NW (~560-660,370-470), zigzag on town/crossing/siege (~370-420) — all read as pen tests.
findings.fixShape: Replace scattered ticks with structured relief (ridge-following hachure runs, form-line chains, terrace steps at the site) in the terrain dress layer; redesign or suppress the mesh/zigzag glyphs. Note for the truth lens: the zigzag cluster also appears on year-018, before the year-19/155 events it sits beside on the base leaf.

findings.title: Organic/low-density fabric is mush — §650 negative-space streets only read in regularized grids
findings.evidence: Viewed village core (buildings/yards/plots merge into one pale texture, internal streets invisible), polycentric (worst: pale plots + pale buildings + sage yards read as crumbled texture), highwater (moth-eaten throughout, MARKET QUARTER zone unreadable), town W-bank. findings.title: Ambiguous glyph vocabulary: water-gate ink blobs, unexplained diamonds/spiral-targets, bald-disc greens, confetti boats

findings.evidence: Viewed town-2, crossing, polycentric: MARKET QUARTER printed twice far apart on each — reads as a labeling bug. town-2/fjord: green field patchwork appears only as abrupt swatches in map corners. crossing: town crammed into bottom ~55%, vast empty N. year-100: the leaf's premise wall is a hairline that under-sells 'the wall stands'.

lists.grade: Totality fails §591 today: the base fabric, roofs, streets-as-negative-space, legends and temporal variants are genuinely strong (several set-pieces are textbook), but six leaves carry wall-law violations, the flagship town family ships a road wash crossing the river beside its bridge, and two leaves are clipped by their own frame — the weakest elements are law-level, not taste-level.

findings.evidence: Viewed crops/t3d-wash-over-water.png (town leaf, svg ~615-650 x 495-540): the main NW-SE road wash continues across the blue as a plain band west of the 3-panel deck, erasing the dark bank line; no ford dashes (intentional fords carry dashed flank lines per bridge-crops/CROP-crossing-FORD-AFTER reference, and the town SVG contains 0 'ford' strings — counted with node). Negative control: highwater's bridge (crops/h2-bridge.png) is textbook §651 — road converges on banks, only the deck spans — proving the correct form exists at this seal.
findings.fixShape: Clip the road-wash polygon at the water body wherever a deck crossing exists, so the wash converges on the deck ends instead of flooding the channel; likely in the road-wash/bridge composition step of the register path that §651 already governs.

findings.title: Walls fail as boundaries: street grids and roads cross unbroken, ungated walls
findings.evidence: Viewed crops/t7-south-context.png (town southern circuit, svg y~850-930): the MARKET QUARTER orthogonal grid continues south across the wall at >=4 aligned street crossings with the wall line unbroken and zero gate glyphs on the whole stretch (manifest gates=2, both elsewhere); buildings flank the continued streets to the frame edge. Same shape confirmed at crossing south wall (crops/c4-south-wall.png, >=2 ungated washes crossing at svg ~(455,970) and ~(523,980)), town-2 north arc (crops/b3-north-gate.png, roads die blindly at the wall aligned inside/outside, no gate on the arc), and polycentric NW (crops/p1-nw-entry.png, main road crosses the unbroken wall at svg ~(360,328); the leaf's single gate is SE). Engine physicalViolations=0 on town — the counter is blind to this class.
findings.fixShape: The wall generator must either cull/reorganize fabric and streets at the ring (walls end districts) or mint a gate at every surviving street crossing; needs a crossing census of streets vs wall rings at build time, in the wall/circuit stage of the register path.

findings.title: Wall circuits truncate mid-field / short of the shore, leaving open flanks
findings.evidence: Viewed crops/c1-wallend-north.png (crossing): the north wall arc dead-ends at a square terminal tower in open field at svg~(505,522), ~18u short of the river, ditch dashes continuing alone, with a street and building row passing around the terminus; the same leaf's west side shows the correct pattern (wall → tower → barred water gate at the channel, crops/c3-west-water.png). Viewed crops/z4-sea-terminus.png (city): SW outer wall stops ~12-19u short of the shore and the coastal road passes ungated around the open end, while the west circuit reaches the sea correctly.
findings.fixShape: Wall termination rule: an open ring must terminate at a water gate on the channel or at the shoreline, never in open ground; extend the terminal segment to the water polygon (or close the ring) in the circuit builder.

findings.title: Corrupted crossing instrument: gate stamp repeated ~8x into a solid black mass (town-2)
findings.evidence: Viewed crops/b1-river-gate.png (town-2, svg ~525-545 x 370-395): where the giant market street crosses the wall, the barred-gate/water-gate stamp is repeated ~8 times overlapping into a ~30x30u solid black caterpillar sitting on dry ground (the river is ~25u west); wall segments stop at the blob and it reads as a black knot even at full view. Correct single-stamp form exists on the same leaf (crops/b2-south-watergate.png).
findings.fixShape: Bound the crossing-glyph stamp count/extent to the actual crossing width and to the presence of water at the crossing point; in the gate/water-gate glyph placement code (L-REG-31/32 territory). Mechanism attribution (stamp-along-path repetition) is PLAUSIBLE — the visual defect is CONFIRMED.

lists.grade: Squint-distance is north-star-competitive, but at the register's own reading distance the drawing hand is missing: streets/markets genuinely close; walls/gates mid; roofs, monuments/churchyards, approaches/countryside far; waterfront farthest (zero shore anatomy on two port settlements).

findings.evidence: Viewed z-city-shore.png (viewBox 200,560,200x200 of city-city-parchment.svg): shore is a bare tint edge — none of hf322's eleven shore-ladder steps (no quay, jetty, mole, hard, slipway, crane, cargo, net racks); the 'port' renders as ~12 plain rotated rectangles floating in the sea in two rows (no hull shape, deck plan, masts, or swing circles per hf265); the shoreline water-gate glyph is an unreadable black lump. Same on fjord leaf (port fact, 2-3 tiny glyphs on the cove). Water surface everywhere is one flat fill + one thalweg line — zero of hf377's twelve textures; no mill/weir/ford drawn on the riverside town asserting 'mill'.
findings.fixShape: A waterfront pass in the register path: shore-edge ladder primitives (quay line+bollards, pile-dot jetty, slipway), hull glyph roster with swing circles, and the hf377 water-texture set (recession lines, stipple bars, current arrows); bind port/landing/mill dossier facts to drawn furniture the way the market square already binds stalls.

findings.title: Roof law absent from fabric — the corpus's own 'without the hand' anti-exemplar row
findings.evidence: z-town-roofs.png (viewBox 215,570,80x80, ~17px/unit): buildings are flat-tinted footprints — no hip lines, two-tone plane shading, chimney squares, jetty dashes, or SE eaves shadow. SVG family isolate (fam-0.3_0.62 overlay) proves ridges exist as 667 faint segments (median 9.2u, max 52.6u) that overshoot eaves and cross open ground, for a roofTarget of 1291; hf208 is the register's #1 fabric law and names this exact look its anti-exemplar.
findings.fixShape: Roof-grammar pass in the fabric renderer: clip ridges to eaves, add hip lines for hipped ends, one-step two-tone plane tint (NW light/SE dark) plus SE eaves shadow tick, chimney squares astride ridges; drop or plot-bound the overshooting segments.

findings.title: Stray grain-line family crosses streets, buildings, the river, and the sea
findings.evidence: SVG path inventory of town-town-parchment.svg: family stroke #2B2118, width 0.25, opacity 0.72 — 814 subpaths of uniform ~25u length; fam-0.25_0.72 overlay render shows them running across streets, through buildings, and over the river; on fjord-town-parchment the same family lays a faint lattice across the open SEA (viewed at 1400px). Corresponds to no corpus mark (hf120 plot-series lines are dashed, per-plot, bounded).
findings.fixShape: Bound these strokes to their parcels (clip to plot polygons, exclude water/street/building masks) or dash them per hf120; a one-layer clipping fix in the renderer where the family is emitted.

findings.title: Monuments are silhouette blobs — plan-complexity rank ladder and churchyard anatomy absent
findings.evidence: z-town-religious.png: great church = solid dark rounded-rect mass, no wall-plan poché, aisles, porch, or cloister (hf323's rule that plan complexity carries rank); churchyard has plain grey circle trees and zero of hf344's items (no south-clustered graves, lych gate, yew, chest tombs, desire-path shortcuts). z-city-civic.png: civic monuments are unidentifiable dark arrow/lump shapes with scratch hatching. Projection is inverted vs corpus: fabric flat while landmark buildings get hip facets (corpus: fabric roofed, monuments wall-plan).
findings.fixShape: Monument renderer switches to wall-plan mode (poché outline, buttress ticks, column-dot arcades, white-when-roofed/hatched-when-ruin interiors) with rank-scaled plan complexity; churchyard sub-pass adds grave ticks south of the nave, lych gate, and specimen-tree crown.

findings.title: Wall dress drawn-but-wrong: railway-band circuit, unseated gates, black-bar water gates, naked ring remnants
findings.evidence: z-town-gateNE.png: band = symmetric double line with square tick ladder (reads as railway; no rubble-fill/coursing per hf261/hf315), gate = bare rounded rectangle floating in a gap — band stops short on both sides, no portcullis dashes or flanking anatomy (hf313); ditch = plain dashed line (corpus: radiating hachure). z-town-watergate.png: water gate = 6-7 fat rounded black bars across the river — the heaviest ink on the plate, no chain boom/winch. City/metropolis inner-ring remnants confirmed in SVG as bare strokes (path 'M73.26 399.14L91.61 488.53M566.74 281.49L542.94 197.89', width 2.47) with no anatomy and no legend row.
findings.fixShape: Wall-band pass: asymmetric band (merlon ticks outer edge only, fill texture between edges), seat gates into the band, portcullis dash pairs, chain-boom water gate, hachured ditch; render old-ring remnants as quarried band stretches with a legend row instead of naked strokes.

findings.title: Countryside/approach furniture layer ~empty: boundary alphabet 1/12, no forests anywhere, gate anatomy 0/12, terrain marks never assemble into landforms
findings.evidence: z-town-fields.png + village/hamlet/thorp/mountain full plates: every field boundary on every leaf is the same thin bare line (hf321's null case; hedges/walls/ditches/pales undrawn); furrow strips are faint hairlines on a minority of village parcels; NO forest masses exist on any of the 18 leaves (hf114 class absent — trees are dot tokens); no windmills, pounds, milestones, wayside crosses, toll bars, or cart queues at any gate (hf311); the noxious-trades belt is correctly sited downstream but carries no discharge plume or smoke — the label does the ink's work (hf267 inverted). Mountain-village relief 0.66 renders as scattered twig scribbles; hachures are connected zigzags, not graded radial strokes (hf112); at 200px squint the mountain terrain vanishes.
